We conducted a longitudinal study using two groups: T1D-prone mice and matched non-diabetic controls. A sample of 60 mice, 30 per group, was monitored from birth to 16 weeks. Bone properties were assessed using high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT) to measure trabecular and cortical parameters in the femur. Additionally, bone strength was evaluated through biomechanical testing. Serum markers of bone turnover, including osteocalcin and C-terminal telopeptide, were measured at weeks 8 and 16. HR-pQCT analysis revealed no significant differences between diabetic and control groups in trabecular thickness, number, or spacing (p > 0.05). Cortical thickness and bone mineral density showed a trend towards lower values in the diabetic group, but these differences did not reach statistical significance (mean difference = 0.03 mm, 95% CI: -0.01 to 0.07, p = 0.08). Biomechanical testing indicated similar ultimate force to failure across groups. Serum markers exhibited comparable patterns in both cohorts, with no significant group differences (p > 0.05). These findings suggest that early-life T1D may not lead to significant alterations in bone microarchitecture or strength in this mouse model.

title: Can a Novel Polyester Mesh Stent Mitigate Neointimal Hyperplasia in Ovine Vein Grafts?
text: This study examined whether a newly developed polyester mesh stent could influence neointimal hyperplasia in vein grafts within a sheep model. Employing a randomized controlled trial design, 18 sheep were assigned to undergo bilateral femoral artery vein graft bypass procedures. Each sheep received one graft with the polyester mesh stent and the other with a traditional bare vein graft, serving as the control. The primary endpoint was the incidence of neointimal hyperplasia, assessed through histological analysis and morphometric measurements at 3 and 6 months post-implantation. Secondary outcomes included graft patency and flow dynamics, monitored using duplex ultrasonography. At 3 months, the polyester mesh stent group exhibited a mean intimal thickness of 0.44±0.09 mm compared to 0.41±0.11 mm in the control group (p=0.47). At 6 months, the intimal thickness was 0.46±0.08 mm versus 0.45±0.10 mm (p=0.52). Graft patency rates were 89% for the stent group and 85% for controls (p=0.67). There was no statistically significant difference in flow volume between the groups at either time point. These findings suggest that while the polyester mesh stent is safe and does not adversely affect graft patency or flow, its impact on reducing neointimal hyperplasia is not statistically significant in this ovine model.

title: Is Chromosome 3 Concordance Observed in Sequential Choroidal Melanoma Biopsies and Resection Specimens?
text: This study aimed to investigate the concordance of chromosome 3 aberrations in choroidal melanoma (CM) through comparative analysis of sequential biopsies and subsequent tumour resection specimens. A prospective cohort of 32 patients, diagnosed with CM at the New York Ocular Oncology Institute from 2010 to 2016, was examined. Chromosome 3 status was assessed using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) array, contingent on the available tissue sample. In 11 cases, genetic assessments were conducted on samples acquired pre- and post-radiotherapy. FISH was performed on 15 biopsy samples, while SNP array analysis was applied to the remaining 17. All 32 resection specimens underwent FISH analysis. Concordance of chromosome 3 status was observed in 23 out of 32 paired biopsy and resection samples. Specifically, 10 of the concordant cases exhibited monosomy 3, while 13 were identified as disomy 3. Among the discordant cases, 5 showed a shift from monosomy 3 in the biopsy to disomy 3 in the resection, and 4 exhibited a transition from disomy 3 to monosomy 3. A notable case demonstrated a loss of chromosome arm 3p in the biopsy with disomy 3 in the resection specimen taken 6 months later. Statistical analysis revealed a concordance rate of 71.9% (95% CI: 54.6-84.5), with a p-value of 0.27, suggesting variability in chromosome 3 aberrations between initial biopsies and subsequent resection specimens.
